ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all shareholders, directors and beneficial owners at the 25% threshold against: (i) domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) under PCMLTFA s. 9.3 and FATF Recommendation 12, with Enhanced Due Diligence triggered by any PEP match; (ii) the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17, and Criminal Code Part II.1 terrorist listings; (iii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists, which are mandatory because the target payment rails (Apple IAP, Paymentwall) settle in USD through US correspondent banking; and (v) EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists where European counterparties are present. Non-face-to-face onboarding and the high-risk digital-content industry classification (ISIC 6311, NAICS 519130 - Medium_Risk_Enhanced) require EDD on source of funds, source of wealth, and corporate-chain integrity. For a real-time video matching and cross-border social telephony app, additional criminal-compliance screening for child exploitation and sexual content indicators is required under the Criminal Code, and payment processors apply merchant integrity and content-moderation screening. Ongoing transaction monitoring and periodic re-screening are mandatory per FINTRAC expectations; the ISC Register must be compiled at incorporation and updated within 15 days of any change in significant control.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) - Corporate Registry Online and authorized Alberta Registry Agents providing subscribed NUANS-format Name Search Reports; official portal: https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry (access via Service Alberta corporate registry agents and eRegistration platform)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Alberta statutory doctrine requires every corporate name to comprise a distinctive element, an optional descriptive element, and a mandatory legal element in Roman/Latin characters. Statutory legal elements are limited to: Limited, Incorporated, Corporation, or the abbreviations Ltd., Inc., Corp.; parallel French forms (Limitee, Incorporee, Compagnie) are accepted where appropriate. Names in non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic) are not entered in the Alberta register; a Roman-character transliteration is mandatory and the transliterated name must be distinguishable on the NUANS search. The name must not be identical or deceptively similar to any existing Alberta or other Canadian corporate name, trade name, or registered trademark per ABCA naming guidelines; punctuation, spaces, and decorative symbols do not confer distinctiveness. A numbered-name fallback (e.g., 1234567 Alberta Ltd.) is available if no clear name is approved.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Loan Corporation, Insurance, Assurance, Reinsurance (prior approval of the federal Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions and/or the Alberta Superintendent of Insurance required)
University, College, Institute, Academy (prior consent of the Alberta Minister of Advanced Education or cognizant regulator required)
Engineer, Engineering, Architect, Lawyer, Legal, Physician, Medical, Doctor, Surgeon, Dentist, Pharmacist (authorization under the applicable Alberta professional statute required)
Royal, Crown, Canada, Alberta, Federal, Provincial (implies government patronage; consent of the Crown or cognizant ministry required)
Co-operative, Co-op (requires incorporation under the Cooperatives Act or prior consent)
Association (implies non-profit or society registration; requires consent or explanatory filing)
Olympic, Olympian, Paralympic (consent of the Canadian Olympic Committee under the Olympic and Paralympic Marks Act)
Condominium (restricted under the Condominium Property Act for corporate name usage)
Chartered, Public, Specialist, Municipal, Police, RCMP (restricted or requiring regulator authorization)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a proposed name by the Registrar: (1) File a written reconsideration request with the Director of Corporations, Service Alberta, within 30 days of the decision, attaching the original NUANS report, a legal argument distinguishing the proposed name from the conflicting mark, and any consent letters (e.g., trademark owner consent); (2) Alternatively, obtain a fresh NUANS Name Search Report with a new distinctive element and re-file the articles of incorporation - this administrative resubmission does not trigger a statutory appeal fee; (3) If the refusal is based on a prohibited or sensitive token, obtain the prior written approval of the cognizant Minister or regulator and resubmit with that approval attached; (4) If administrative remedies are exhausted, commence an application for judicial review before the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Alberta Rules of Court, AR 124/2010, within six months of the final refusal, naming the Director of Corporations as respondent; the court may order the Registrar to accept the name or direct re-consideration. Practically, most rejections are resolved by re-filing with a more distinctive element, avoiding judicial review costs.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible with material caveats. ABCA requires the registered office to be a physical street address in Alberta at which service of process can be effected and corporate records may be kept; a post office box alone is statutorily invalid. A commercial virtual office with a physical mailing address and meeting room, or a law-firm registered-office suite, satisfies the statute. However, a pure virtual office without leased premises will increase non-face-to-face CDD friction during merchant onboarding with Apple IAP and Paymentwall, bank account opening, and CRA assessment of the place of effective management for tax residence. For this digital video-match social app with no local physical retail footprint, the recommended structure is a bundled physical virtual office in Calgary or Edmonton plus a professional registered-office and records-custody agent.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - estimated less than 3% annualized probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by the Alberta Registrar for a pure digital-services operating entity; moderate probability (approximately 10-15%) of an announced CRA desk audit relating to GST registration, corporate income tax, or payroll; FINTRAC site-visit risk is negligible unless the entity is separately classified as a money services business, which is not anticipated under the Apple IAP and Paymentwall settlement structure; however, banking and payment-processor CDD may nonetheless require proof of physical premises occupancy.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, as amended; ss. 5 (incorporation), 6 (articles of incorporation), 9 (certificate of incorporation), 23 (directors), 101 (registered office), 111 (meetings), 516 (electronic records).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Corporate Registry (ACRS Online)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) and Initial Notice of Directors (Form 2); Certificate of Incorporation issued under the Alberta Business Corporations Act
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is prescribed; incorporators may designate authorized share capital in the articles. No escrow account or paid-up capital deposit is required for an ordinary Alberta business corporation formation, except where a prospectus or exempt-market capital raising triggers securities rules under the Alberta Securities Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation of the Company under the Alberta Business Corporations Act be ratified; that the Articles of Incorporation filed on the date of filing and the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Alberta Corporate Registry be accepted; that the authorized share capital and special rights attaching to issued shares be confirmed; that the registered office be established at the address set out in the Articles and the registered office record keeper be appointed; that the directors named in the Initial Notice of Directors be confirmed; that the President, Secretary, and Treasurer be appointed as the initial officers; that banking signatories and corporate account authorities be designated; and that the incorporator and officers be authorized to execute ancillary filings, notices, registers, and governance records necessary to operationalize the Company. RESOLVED FURTHER, that digital signatures be accepted for all subsequent filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, through ACRS Online or an approved NUANS provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name search request to obtain a NUANS name search report; confirm that the proposed distinctive element and corporate indicator are acceptable; reserve the name electronically, if required, before filing incorporation documents.
required_dossiers: Completed corporate name search request form
Proposed English and, if desired, French corporate name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is confusing or unavailable, select an alternate name from the reserved list or file a request for name reservation extension and re-submit the name search.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Articles of Incorporation and Initial Notice of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, Corporate Registry (ACRS Online)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Form 1 Articles of Incorporation specifying authorized share capital, classes of shares, restrictions on share transfers, number of directors, full registered office address in Alberta, and all directors' names and residential addresses. Prepare Form 2 Initial Notice of Directors. Ensure the first directors consent to act in writing and that all required signatures are dated and digitally authenticated.
required_dossiers: Disposition of pre-incorporation contract or agreement, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice, correct the flagged fields and re-file within the stated correction period; pay any applicable re-filing fee and keep the original submission date by responding to the request promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Dossiers and Pay Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, ACRS Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed Articles and Notice of Directors, remit the prescribed filing fee, and submit the application through the ACRS electronic system; retain an electronic filing receipt until the Certificate of Incorporation is issued.
required_dossiers: Completed Form 2 Initial Notice of Directors
Electronic or paper authorization and contact details of the filer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected or queried, obtain the written rejection reason, amend the Articles or Notice accordingly, and re-file; resubmit with corrected information within the registry's specified deadline to preserve the desired effective date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receive Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Key
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, obtain the official Certificate of Incorporation together with the corporate registration number and, where applicable, the ACRS corporate access key; verify that the certificate, official name, and registered office address match the filed Articles.
required_dossiers: Electronic copy of the filed Articles
Corporate registry receipt and corporate identification record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a typographical error, apply for a certificate of correction from the Alberta Corporate Registry and submit substantiating documents within the registry's correction window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Federal Tax and Payroll Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) through Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the corporate name, corporation number, and Certificate of Incorporation, register for the nine-digit Business Number, corporate income tax account, GST/HST account, and any payroll deduction accounts if the Company will have employees; complete online authentication and select the applicable programs.
required_dossiers: Corporate name, address, and fiscal year-end
Directors' first name and date of birth details for authentication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the business number is not generated, contact CRA Business Enquiries to correct filer or company data and request manual account activation while maintaining a reference number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Corporate Governance Records and Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate Secretary and Registered Office Record Keeper; notarial or legal counsel acting locally
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first directors' meeting to adopt by-laws, resolve on share subscriptions and share certificates, establish a registered office record book, confirm officers, prescribe the banking arrangement, and approve transaction authorizations; place the Certificate of Incorporation, Articles, Notices of Directors, by-laws, consents, share register, and transfer ledger in the corporate minute book.
required_dossiers: Minute book, share certificates, and corporate seal, if adopted
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an enrolled instrument is inconsistent with the filed Articles or statutory requirements, ratify correcting resolutions and amend the minute book entries with board and shareholder consent, as applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 6311 digital data processing and application hosting; for any occupied Alberta office, municipal municipal development and building safety authorities under the Alberta Safety Codes Act apply.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable; no industrial or manufacturing operating permit is required for a real-time video matching and social telephony application business operating as a data-processing and software-services corporation.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEP) — not triggered for this office-based digital services operation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt; no Environmental Impact Assessment or registration under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act (EPEA) is required for the described non-manufacturing software and remote data services business.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; the business generates no wastewater discharge, no measurable VOC emissions, and no industrial waste stream. If physical office premises are used, municipal sanitary sewer bylaws, building code ventilation requirements, and Alberta OHS rules respecting indoor air quality and electronic equipment disposal apply.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupational Health and Safety Act, RSA 2000, c O-2 compliance required; fire safety certification under Alberta Fire Code and municipal fire authority for leased premises; structural load and egress inspections under Alberta Building Code; electrical and elevator safety clearances administered by Alberta Municipal Affairs, Safety Services Division; workplace first-aid and emergency evacuation clearances required before staff occupy the office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA). Federal indirect tax administration and corporate income tax administration for Alberta under the Tax Administration Agreement with the Government of Alberta. Portals: GST/HST NETFILE via My Business Account (canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses.html) and Business Registration Online (BRO).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A federal or Alberta-incorporated business corporation must obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN) from CRA. Foreign entities may register via postal application on Form RC1 'Request for a Business Number', by telephone through the Business Window, or online through Business Registration Online. The GST/HST account is opened concurrently; a non-resident corporation supplying digital services in Canada is also required to complete the simplified non-resident registration under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act. Alberta imposes no provincial sales tax, and all Alberta corporate tax filings are administered through CRA, eliminating separate provincial registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Canadian business corporation is resident in Canada under common law (central management and control) and taxable under Income Tax Act s. 2(1) on worldwide income; it is not a pass-through entity under any federal or Alberta statute. Closed or closely held corporations may elect the Canadian-Controlled Private Corporation (CCPC) status if the parent is a qualifying Canadian resident; a foreign parent of a video app corporation will typically render the subsidiary a non-CCPC, losing the small business deduction. No tax-consolidated group filing is permitted except the lifetime capital gains exemption transfer and related entity elections.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not employ the US check-the-box regime; a corporation is always a separate taxable person. Relevant elections include: (i) s. 156 Excise Tax Act election to treat a closely related group of registrants as a single GST/HST registrant; (ii) ETA s. 238(2) election to file GST/HST annually when all supplies are zero-rated (including cross-border video matching services); (iii) Income Tax Act s. 18.4/18.6 and s. 95(5.1) hybrid mismatch elections for controlled foreign affiliates to neutralize double non-taxation; and (iv) s. 152(4) designation election for the computation of foreign accrual property income. For Alberta, no separate provincial S elections exist given the single-administration regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST – Goods and Services Tax, Harmonized Sales Tax under Part IX, Excise Tax Act (R.S.C. 1985, c. E-15)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 – GST registration is mandatory once worldwide taxable supplies in Canada (excluding zero-rated exports) exceed CAD 30,000 in any single calendar quarter or in a series of four consecutive quarters (s. 148 ETA small supplier threshold; for non-resident digital service providers, the same CAD 30,000 quarterly threshold applies to specified supplies under the regime at ss. 211.1–211.18 ETA).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, mandatory digital stamping, or API-based government preclearance exists for GST/HST. The CRA requires prescribed disclosure on invoices (seller's BN, date, supplier and recipient names, description, consideration, tax status of the supply; s. 221 ETA and Reg. 242). Electronic invoicing is permitted without prior authorization under the pan-Canadian Peppol BIS 3.0 standard, which remains voluntary for B2B exchanges. GST/HST returns are filed electronically via NETFILE, and for non-resident simplified registrants, through the dedicated web portal. Records must be retained electronically for six years and made available for CRA audit in a readable format.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A registrant operating a real-time video matching and cross-border social telephony application may apply the zero-rate (GST/HST 0%) to supplies of services made to non-resident recipients where the supply is deemed to be made outside Canada under s. 142.1(1)(d) ETA, or where the service qualifies under Part V, Schedule VI (services supplied to a non-resident, other than services in respect of real property in Canada or physical goods in Canada). The zero-rating applies irrespective of the commercial payment model (subscription, virtual gifts, advertisement sponsorship) provided the recipient is a non-resident and the performance of the service does not occur at a place in Canada at the time of supply. Supplies to users physically present in Canada are standard-rated at 5% and require a Canadian GST/HST charge; corporate income tax on export profits is otherwise shielded by the federal 'supply of services to non-residents' rules only for GST purposes, not for income tax, so transfer pricing documentation for a foreign parent or associated platforms is essential.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration for any ancillary physical exports (SD on CAED) or proof that export is of services where no customs declaration is applicable; for digital services the equivalent is the service contract or subscription agreement
GST/HST zero-rated commercial invoice showing BN, date, description of the video matching service, and a legend 'Zero-rated supply to non-resident — Part V, Schedule VI, ETA'
Bill of Lading or airway bill (only where incidental hardware/media is shipped) plus service performance logs demonstrating the app server's Canadian IP origin
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank SWIFT/MT103 records evidencing foreign currency settlement received from Apple IAP and Paymentwall payment rails
Non-residence evidence of the end user: billing country attribute, geolocation IP logs, or payment card country code retained in the BSS/OSS system
RC4640 or Form T1134 related-party disclosure where the foreign parent is the contracting counterparty, to support arm's length consideration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA subjects zero-rated export claims to audit under s. 296 ETA, with a four-year normal reassessment window (s. 298(1)) that is extended indefinitely where a taxpayer has made any misrepresentation attributable to fraud, neglect, or wilful default. Penalties: s. 280 failure-to-register/collect penalty of 5% of net GST, increased by 1% per month up to 12 months; a penalty equal to the amount of improperly claimed input tax credits under s. 285.2; and a 10% 'civil penalty for false statements' under s. 285.1. Criminal tax evasion under s. 327 ETA is punishable on summary conviction by a fine up to CAD 100,000 and/or imprisonment up to one year, and on indictment by a fine up to 200% of the evaded GST and/or imprisonment up to five years, for export zero-rating fraud such as synthetic non-resident users, circular invoicing through a shell foreign intermediary, or deliberate destruction of geolocation evidence. Where export proceeds are not repatriated to Canada within the 180-day window, the outstanding balance is treated as a shareholder or intercompany loan subject to s. 15(2)/90(2) income inclusion, foreign accrual property income attribution under s. 91, and Canadian-dollar translation gains under s. 261 are taxed; CRA exchange rate revaluation can also trigger reassessments of the GST refund base.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) exercises monetary policy and currency issuance; exchange-control competency is residual under the Minister of Finance pursuant to the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52) and the Bretton Woods and Related Agreements Act. FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada) administers cross-border currency monitoring and AML/CTF reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). OSFI supervises deposit-taking bank conduct.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full Article VIII IMF convertibility with no exchange-control licensing for either current or capital account transactions. Capital inflows, repatriations, dividends, and profit remittances are unrestricted in mechanism; practical hurdles are tax-based: (i) Part XIII withholding tax of 25% on dividends/royalties payable to non-residents unless reduced by an applicable treaty (e.g., US/UK treaty rates 5% or 15%); (ii) Investment Canada Act (ICA) review if a foreign investor later acquires control of a Canadian business above statutory financial thresholds, with a separate national security review for sensitive digital media businesses; (iii) for the Alberta entity, the Income Tax Act requires conversion of all foreign-currency revenue into CAD for reporting unless a section 261 functional-currency election (generally USD) is made.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada repealed mandatory foreign-exchange surrender with the abolition of the Foreign Exchange Control Act in 1951; there is no statutory repatriation window, minimum holding period, or forced conversion ratio for export service receipts, including digital net settlements from Apple IAP or Paymentwall. The Alberta company may lawfully retain USD/EUR in Canadian-chartered foreign-currency accounts. De facto obligations arise solely from tax reporting, transfer-pricing arm's-length documentation, and CRA functional-currency rules, not from any surrender regime.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM, supplementary-only (never as primary treasury). Legal constraints: the Bank Act (s. 972.2) prohibits unauthorized deposit-taking in Canada, so an offshore EMI such as Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, or Mercury may provide Canadian-dollar custodial sub-accounts only if it is a FINTRAC-registered Money Service Business (MSB) under PCMLTFA or partners with a Schedule I bank as an authorized agent. For this specific video-match app, the company is properly classified as a merchant (not an MSB) because all end-user payments are captured by Apple IAP and Paymentwall; the firm merely receives net settlements. Permitted structure: maintain one FINTRAC-registered EMI account (e.g., Wise Business) for low-cost USD/EUR corridor liquidity and small creator payouts, capped at under 5% of monthly treasury flow, with the main balance ledgered at a Tier 1 chartered bank to avoid unlicensed deposit risk and to satisfy banking due diligence on the entity's principal account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical branch visit or live video-verified identity meeting is generally required for at least one full director, or, in the alternative, a Canadian-resident authorized signing officer appointed by board resolution. Fully remote onboarding is not available for a new entity characterized as Medium_Risk_Enhanced with non-resident ownership. Recommended Alberta path: (i) the founding director attends an in-person Calgary/Edmonton commercial banking appointment with a relationship manager; (ii) non-resident directors without travel capability submit notarized passports and proof-of-address, executed alongside a local signing-officer mandate; (iii) the bank requires the Alberta Corporate Registry certificate of status, Articles of Incorporation, and completed beneficial ownership schedule; (iv) onboarding timeline is 2-4 weeks, ending with a mandatory first-transaction review before any wire outbound is released.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity digital micro-transactions via Apple IAP and Paymentwall flagged as a potential money-laundering channel through in-app credit purchases, chargebacks, and digital gift cards.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Current App Store/Google Play listing and public terms of service; (ii) executed Apple and Paymentwall merchant processing agreements demonstrating that end-user KYC and screening are performed by the processors; (iii) transaction-flow diagram showing the company as a downstream merchant only, not a money transmitter; (iv) voluntary PCMLTFA s.10 AML/CTF program; (v) chargeback and refund policy; (vi) geoblocking and sanctions-screening policy for user IP addresses and merchant jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border social telephony creates exposure to sanctioned persons or jurisdictions (UN Act, Special Economic Measures Act, OFAC-listed counterparties) via international user traffic.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Sanctions-screening implementation log against the Canadian Consolidated Autonomous Sanctions List and OFAC SDN list; (ii) evidence of IP-geoblocking for prohibited regions; (iii) content-moderation and age-verification protocols; (iv) compliance attestation from Alberta legal counsel; (v) monthly no-exposure reporting to the account manager.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership and potential nominee-shareholder opacity triggers Enhanced Due Diligence, PEP screening, and UBO verification requirements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Notarized UBO register identifying all shareholders with more than 25% ownership, including DOB and country of tax residence; (ii) certificate of status from the Alberta Corporate Registry; (iii) current organizational chart certified by the corporate secretary; (iv) source-of-wealth letters and bank references for material shareholders; (v) declaration confirming no senior foreign political figures are involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid inbound capital injection in the first 90 days after incorporation flagged as a possible money-muling or layering transaction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Board resolution specifically authorizing the share issuance and escrow release; (ii) executed share subscription agreement; (iii) SWIFT MT103 trail showing the remitter is the exact shareholder named in the registry; (iv) escrow release instruction countersigned by Alberta counsel; (v) capital schedule filed under the Alberta Business Corporations Act; (vi) a solicitor's closing file confirming no undisclosed liens or third-party pledges.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign shareholders wire via SWIFT MT103 directly to the company's designated USD or CAD account at the Canadian chartered bank (e.g., RBC SWIFT ROYCCAT2, TD SWIFT TDOMCATTTOR). Remittance field 70 should state 'SHARE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' and field 72 should reference the board resolution date. Canada requires no regulatory pre-approval and no purpose-code permit; the receiving bank records the inward credit under standard corporate account treatment. For amounts above CAD 100,000 the bank performs EDD verification linking the remitter to the corporate registry and UBO schedule. An Investment Canada Act notification is not required for greenfield incorporation or organic share subscription of the Alberta operating entity, but if a foreign investor subsequently acquires control of an existing Canadian business, ICA net-benefit or national-security review may apply. The escrowed capital is releasable only against a director's sworn declaration and solicitor's undertaking, then moved via internal book transfer to the operating ledger.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For recurring operating payments — cloud infrastructure (AWS/Azure), advertising (Google/Meta), and optional creator payouts — the company will use (i) SWIFT MT103 for all non-Canadian beneficiaries, including beneficiary bank BIC, and IBAN or ABA destination codes, with CAD/USD conversion executed at the bank's FX rate at payment time; (ii) Payments Canada Lynx and Real-Time Rail for domestic CAD disbursements to Alberta vendors; (iii) confirmed irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (UCP 600 / ISBP 745) for material license contracts above CAD 100,000 where the supplier requires documentary security; (iv) a weekly sweep protocol to convert excess USD net settlement balances from Apple and Paymentwall into CAD, using the bank's automated FX conversion pool. For inbound processor settlements, the company should instruct Paymentwall and Apple to route via ACH (USD) or SWIFT (EUR/USD) to the Tier 1 account, maintaining a clear audit trail of platform fees, refunds, and net revenue.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable CAD/USD FX forwards (maturity up to 12 months) executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with credit support annex at a Schedule I Canadian bank, designated for hedge accounting under IFRS 9 if documentation requirements are met.
FX swaps and swap-point rollovers to align the liquidity timing between USD inflows from Apple IAP/Paymentwall and USD-denominated payables to AWS, Google, and licensed content providers.
Vanilla FX options, including zero-premium participations and collars (risk reversals), purchased from the bank's treasury desk to cap USD purchase cost for marketing and infrastructure spend.
Spot conversions executed through the bank's electronic FX platform with a standing instruction to auto-convert net USD settlements to CAD within 48 hours of receipt.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only for documented underlying exposure in a non-convertible currency; for a CAD/USD treasury profile, a deliverable forward is the cleaner and standard instrument, and any NDF would require independent legal confirmation of the underlying exposure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the anniversary date of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No late fee applies, but failure to file for one year triggers a Registrar's notice of administrative dissolution; reinstatement requires an application and payment of reinstatement fees.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including Alberta provincial corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Return due within 6 months after fiscal year-end; tax balance due within 2 months after fiscal year-end for a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) and within 3 months otherwise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty is 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month (maximum 12 months). Repeated failure carries a 10% or 20% penalty. Daily compound interest applies to unpaid balances and penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Director and Registered Office Update (filed as part of the Alberta Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same anniversary-based window: within 60 days after incorporation or amalgamation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Incomplete or incorrect updates may be rejected; knowingly false statements are offenses under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) and may lead to fines or director disqualification.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An Alberta private business corporation is not required to appoint an auditor unless: (1) it is an offering corporation whose securities are publicly traded; (2) shareholders holding at least 5% of the issued voting shares make a written requisition; or (3) a supervising regulator applies audit requirements because of the corporation's business sector.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public enterprises; ASPE (Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook) for private enterprises; both are recognized generally accepted accounting principles in Canada.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta law does not require an annual UBO filing to the corporate registry. However, a non-offering Alberta corporation must maintain an internal Register of Significant Individuals (RSI) identifying any individual holding 25% or more of voting shares or fair market value, or otherwise exercising control. The register must be updated within 15 days of any change, including a share transfer, and must be produced upon request by law enforcement, tax authorities, or the Registrar.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined general corporate rate (15.0% federal Part I under ITA s. 123(1) plus 8.0% Alberta general rate under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act). A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) benefits from an 11.0% combined small business rate (9.0% federal plus 2.0% Alberta) on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: CCPC small business deduction on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income derived from the video-matching app's in-app purchases and subscriptions. Federal SR&ED refundable investment tax credit up to 35% for qualifying research and development in real-time video matching and AI algorithms. Alberta Capital Investment Tax Credit (20% refundable) for eligible investments. Non-resident-controlled private corporations are disqualified from the small business deduction and face a flat 23.0% combined rate.
